questions.prompt: The default access for a class member (no modifier) is:
To expose data safely while keeping the field hidden, use a:
Fill in the blank to make a class only usable within its assembly
questions.explanation: internal restricts the type to the assembly.

questions.prompt: A public method in an internal class is effectively accessible:
options: Only within the assembly (class limits it)
questions.explanation: The less accessible member (the class) bounds the method.

questions.prompt: Define class Account with private decimal Balance=100 and public void Deposit(decimal a){Balance+=a;} and public decimal Get(){return Balance;} then deposit 25 and print Get()
questions.explanation: Encapsulated balance mutated via public method.

questions.prompt: Which modifier allows access only within the program text of the containing type?
questions.explanation: private is confined to the declaring type.

questions.prompt: Arrange to expose a private field via a property
items: public int N { get { return n; } set { n = value; } }

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank to restrict a member to the containing class and derived classes
Accessibility of a member is limited by the:
options: Less accessible of the type or member
questions.explanation: The containing type bounds member visibility.
